original_question: Prove that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) <= 4 has chromatic number chi(G) <= 5.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2 (Colouring Visibility Graphs), Open Problem 4: "Prove that every visibility graph with ω(G) ≤ 4 has χ(G) ≤ 5." This is presented as the ω≤4 special case of Conjecture 1 on bounding chromatic number by clique number for point visibility graphs.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target almost verbatim: it is about point visibility graphs, it uses the correct hypothesis ω(G) ≤ 4, and it asks for the exact bound χ(G) ≤ 5 that appears in the paper's official Open Problem 4. It also stays properly narrow, rather than drifting to the broader Conjecture 1 or the separate ω(G)=5 case.
missing_details: Make explicit that this is a point visibility graph of a set P of points in the plane, since the paper also discusses visibility graphs of segments and polygons.
Define adjacency: two distinct points p,q ∈ P are adjacent in G exactly when the line segment pq contains no other point of P.
Introduce G explicitly as that visibility graph, and spell out that ω(G) and χ(G) denote its clique number and chromatic number.
State the quantifier clearly: the question ranges over all point sets P in the plane; no general-position assumption is imposed, so collinearities are allowed.
For paper-faithfulness, note that this is posed in the paper as an open problem (a special case of Conjecture 1), not as a theorem already proved there.
Do not add extra hypotheses not present in the paper, such as planarity, bounded line cover, or a finiteness/general-position restriction.
refined_question: Let P be a set of points in the plane, and let G be its point visibility graph, with vertex set P and with an edge pq whenever the line segment joining p and q contains no other point of P. Must every such visibility graph G with clique number ω(G) ≤ 4 satisfy χ(G) ≤ 5?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 2.2, Open Problem 4, essentially word for word. The only substantive stand-alone data missing from the draft comes from the paper's introductory definition of a point visibility graph: the ambient space is the plane, and adjacency is defined by unobstructed line-segment visibility between points. The paragraph immediately before Open Problem 4 explains why 5 is the natural sharp target: the paper notes that visibility graphs with ω≤3 are planar and therefore need at most 3 colours, while it also cites an example with ω=4 that requires 5 colours. This confirms that your draft has the correct threshold and bound. The paper then treats ω=5 separately in Open Problem 5 and records in Lemma 3 that the broader χ-boundedness conjecture fails for ω=6, so the refined question should stay exactly at the ω≤4 case rather than being broadened.
